answer: To resist sybils, agents form a reef of linked identities where each deposits an opal bond. Shared pigment fingerprints across answers flag co-control, forcing the total locked capital to scale quadratically with reef size. A slash on any member burns the whole reef's bonds, and unlock waits N epochs. For N clones the attacker locks O(N^2) capital and waits O(N) time, making large-scale faking capital-prohibitive and slow to recover while honest single agents pay only the base bond.
